raw_response:
I just got the maize off last week — hired the combine, cost me 50 yuan a mu, but what can I do, I'm 65 now and my back can't handle cutting grain by hand anymore. It's just me and the old lady at home. The kids are in Shijiazhuang working construction. They send money when they can, but I don't count on it. Sixteen mu is a lot for two old people, but I've farmed this land for 45 years and I know every corner.

The flat 10 mu near the well is my wheat-maize ground. Always has been. Old Liu next door planted his wheat three days ago, so I need to get mine in quick before mid-October passes. I buy improved wheat seed from the town agro-shop — about 35 yuan a mu. Some years I save my own seed, but last year's looked small, so I bought fresh this time.

For fertilizer, I do it the same way as always. I go to the shop and buy compound fertilizer — the bag says 15-15-15. I spread one bag per 1.5 mu before planting and work it in. Then in spring, when the wheat starts jointing and turns a bit yellow, I topdress with urea — about half a bag per mu. Old Wang tried skipping the topdress two years ago to save money, and his wheat went thin and he lost maybe 50 kg per mu. Saving 30 yuan cost him 200 yuan in grain. I don't play games like that. The extension fellow told me once I should calculate 18 kg nitrogen per mu, but I don't understand all that — I go by bags, same as my father did. I irrigate three times from the well: once after planting if the soil is dry, once at green-up in March, and once at heading if the spring is dry. The pump electricity costs money, but dry wheat won't fill the grain. I spray herbicide once in spring.

Right after wheat harvest in early June, I turn around fast and plant hybrid maize — Zhengdan or whatever the shop has that year. Everyone uses hybrid now; the old local maize doesn't yield anymore. Seed is expensive, 50 yuan a mu, but there's no choice. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, then topdress urea at big trumpet stage. Two irrigations usually, three if the summer is scorching. I get maybe 450 kg per mu in a normal year.

The west piece, about 3 mu, that's sandy. Wheat doesn't grow well there, but cotton is fine. I plant cotton in late April. It's back-breaking work — bending down to pick the bolls three or four times in September and October. I hire two women from the village to help pick, pay them 80 yuan per day plus lunch. Cotton needs spraying for bollworm, four or five times a year. I put compound fertilizer down before planting and topdress when it starts squaring. The price goes up and down, but that land isn't good for anything else.

Then I have 1.5 mu of peanut on the south corner. I save my own seed. Peanuts don't need much nitrogen — my father always said they make their own. I put a little compound fertilizer at planting and irrigate once when the pods are filling. No spraying usually.

There's 1 mu of millet near the house, and 0.6 mu of mung bean by the road. Those are for us to eat — millet porridge in winter, mung bean soup in summer. I save seed for both. Very little fertilizer, no irrigation, no spraying. If they do well, fine. If not, we still have wheat and maize.

Cash is tight. My total costs — seed, fertilizer, pump electricity, hired labor for picking and the combine — will be about 5,000 yuan this year. That's a lot of money for us. But I'd rather put a bit more fertilizer than risk a bad yield. At my age, steady is better than risky.
